quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: Which motherboard form factor is smaller than ATX and commonly fits in an ATX case?
option_b: E-ATX
explanation: microATX is smaller than ATX and many ATX cases include its mounting pattern.
source_name: Nexus curriculum team (adapted from permitted ExamCompass legacy bank: Motherboard Quiz)

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: What must be checked before placing a CPU into a replacement motherboard?
option_b: Socket chipset and firmware support
explanation: Socket fit alone is insufficient; chipset and firmware must support the CPU.
source_name: Nexus curriculum team (adapted from permitted ExamCompass legacy bank: CPU Quiz)

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: What is the safest action if a CPU does not drop into its socket with almost no force?
option_b: Stop and verify alignment and socket compatibility
explanation: A compatible aligned CPU seats without force; forcing it can damage pins or contacts.

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: Why is thermal compound used between a CPU and heatsink?
option_b: To fill microscopic gaps and improve heat transfer
explanation: Thermal compound fills air gaps so heat transfers efficiently to the cooler.
source_name: Nexus curriculum team (adapted from permitted ExamCompass legacy bank: CPU Quiz)

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: A PC shuts down only during CPU-intensive work. Which observation is most useful first?
option_b: CPU temperature and CPU-fan operation
explanation: The workload-specific shutdown makes processor temperature and cooling operation the most direct first evidence.
source_name: Nexus curriculum team (adapted from permitted ExamCompass legacy bank: Core PC Hardware Troubleshooting Quiz)

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: Which slot is normally used for a modern discrete graphics card?
option_b: DIMM
explanation: Discrete graphics cards normally use a PCI Express x16 physical slot.
source_name: Nexus curriculum team (adapted from permitted ExamCompass legacy bank: Motherboard Quiz)

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: A newly installed graphics card is detected but fails under load. Which TWO hardware checks are most relevant before changing software?
option_a: Verify required auxiliary GPU power is fully seated
option_b: Compare the PSU capacity/connectors with the card requirements
explanation: A card can enumerate on slot power yet fail under load when auxiliary power is missing or the PSU cannot meet its requirements.

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: Which check specifically addresses physical compatibility for an expansion card?
option_b: Case clearance and bracket size
explanation: A card must fit the case and bracket area; lane bandwidth drivers and power are separate compatibility checks.

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: After installing a network expansion card what is the strongest verification?
option_b: Device Manager is clean and the original network task succeeds
explanation: Recognition plus an end-to-end user task verifies both installation and function.

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: What does a modular power supply provide?
option_b: Detachable power cables
explanation: Modular PSUs allow unused cables to be detached; their PSU-side pinouts are not universal.
source_name: Nexus curriculum team (adapted from permitted ExamCompass legacy bank: Power Supply Quiz)

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: Why should a modular cable from a different PSU model not be reused without manufacturer confirmation?
option_a: The connector latch may face the other direction
option_b: PSU-side pinouts can differ and damage components
option_c: Detachable cables always carry less current
option_d: The cable changes the PSU efficiency rating
explanation: Connectors may look identical while PSU-side wiring differs; use only a cable explicitly compatible with the exact PSU.

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: Which connector powers the motherboard itself on a typical ATX system?
option_b: SATA data
explanation: The main ATX motherboard connection is normally 24-pin.

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: A replacement PSU has enough total wattage but lacks the connector required by the graphics card. Is it suitable?
option_a: Yes because total wattage is the only requirement
option_b: No because connector compatibility is also required
option_c: Yes if a SATA-to-GPU adapter is added without vendor approval
option_d: No because every graphics card requires the same connector
explanation: Wattage alone is insufficient; the PSU must provide the required approved connectors and power delivery.

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: What should a technician do with a failed desktop PSU enclosure?
option_a: Open it and replace a capacitor
option_b: Replace the unit and never open the enclosure
explanation: PSUs contain hazardous stored energy and are replaced as units by support technicians.

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: Why leave sensible wattage headroom when selecting a PSU?
option_a: To guarantee the PSU always runs silently
option_b: To handle peak load and avoid continuous operation at the limit
option_c: To make a lower efficiency rating equivalent to a higher one
option_d: To remove the need to check GPU power connectors
explanation: Reasonable headroom supports transient/peak demand and avoids sizing the PSU exactly at the calculated limit; it does not replace compatibility checks.

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: Which THREE preparations belong in an approved internal desktop upgrade?
option_a: Confirm backup approval and rollback plan
option_b: Shut down, unplug, and follow the device discharge procedure
option_c: Use ESD controls and record cable locations
option_d: Leave mains power connected while moving components
option_e: Open the PSU to confirm its capacitor condition
explanation: Approval and rollback planning protect the service; power isolation and ESD/connection controls protect people data and equipment.

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: Why photograph and label connections before a motherboard replacement?
option_b: To support correct reconnection and rollback
explanation: A connection record reduces wiring mistakes and supports rollback.

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: Which source is strongest for a system-specific motherboard replacement procedure?
option_b: The manufacturer's service manual
explanation: The vendor service manual documents model-specific sequence and compatibility.

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: A component is installed and appears in firmware. What still needs verification?
option_b: Operating-system recognition and the original user requirement
explanation: End-to-end verification must include OS and original task behavior.

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: When troubleshooting after an upgrade why change one logical thing at a time?
option_b: It preserves cause-and-effect evidence
explanation: Controlled changes let the technician attribute the result to a specific action.

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: What Windows tool can identify the current motherboard/system model and hardware summary?
explanation: System Information is launched with msinfo32.

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: What anti-static protection acronym describes controls used to prevent electrostatic discharge damage?
explanation: ESD means electrostatic discharge and names the protection practice.

quiz_title: A+ PC Components, Power & Safe Upgrades — Module Bank
question_text: What motherboard expansion interface normally carries a modern graphics card? Give the interface and common lane size.
explanation: PCI Express x16 is the expected answer.
